extra_misconceptions.fact: A stall occurs whenever the wing exceeds its critical angle of attack, which can happen at any airspeed or flight attitude.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An airplane stalls only when its forward airspeed drops below a fixed number of knots, regardless of wing angle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rudder pedals control yaw around the vertical axis, while pulling back on the yoke or stick moves the elevator to pitch the nose up.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling back on the rudder pedals raises the airplane's nose to initiate a climb during normal flight.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thrust propels the aircraft forward against drag, while airflow over the wing's airfoil generates upward lift to oppose weight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Engine thrust directly lifts a fixed-wing aircraft upward into the sky against the pull of gravity.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The attitude indicator relies on an internal spinning gyroscope or solid-state AHRS sensors, not pitot-static air pressure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: The attitude indicator measures aircraft pitch and bank angles by sensing outside barometric air pressure changes.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to an airplane's roll and yaw axes when the pilot deflects the left aileron upward and the right aileron downward?
Which physical mechanism allows a helicopter rotor to generate lift while hovering at zero forward airspeed unlike a fixed wing?
What measurement on the altimeter's Kollsman window must a pilot set before takeoff to read accurate altitude above sea level?
Why is it dangerous to fly with a blocked pitot tube even if the static port remains completely clear of ice or debris?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Launching too steeply or forcefully causes the glider to stall and dive; a gentle, level throw near stall speed maximizes glide.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Throwing a foam plate glider as hard as possible with the nose pointed straight up produces the longest glide distance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Downward elevons increase lift at the tail and pitch the nose down, whereas upward elevons push the tail down and raise the nose.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Bending both trailing-edge elevons downward on an FPG-9 glider causes the nose to pitch upward into a climb.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A tail-heavy center of gravity makes a model unstable and prone to sudden stalls; the balance point belongs near the forward wing spar.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding clay weight to the tail of a nose-heavy model until it balances behind the wing improves longitudinal stability.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unpowered hand-glide tests must come first so trim errors can be corrected gently before full propeller torque causes a crash.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Winding a balsa airplane's rubber motor to maximum tension on the first test flight is the best way to check wing alignment.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to your FPG-9 glider's flight path if both elevons are bent slightly upward before a hand launch?
Under what condition does shifting a model airplane's center of gravity too far aft behind the wing cause unstable flight?
What measurement confirms your balsa model achieved a true 25-foot straight-line flight rather than a wide turning arc?
Where should a Scout position spectators and patrol members before launching a wound balsa model or remote-controlled aircraft?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Water is denser than aviation fuel and settles at the bottom of the tank, where it must be drained from sump valves before flight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Water contamination in aviation gasoline floats on top of the fuel and evaporates harmlessly through the tank vents.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Aircraft magnetos are self-contained engine-driven generators that can fire spark plugs even when the battery switch is completely off.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Turning off the aircraft master battery switch disables the engine magnetos and prevents the propeller from firing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: On a stabilized final approach, pitch attitude primarily controls airspeed while power adjustments control the rate of descent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: During a landing approach, pilots control their descent path strictly with the elevator and control airspeed only with throttle.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Written preflight checklists are mandatory to prevent omission errors such as leaving pitot covers, control locks, or fuel caps loose.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A visual walkaround without a printed checklist is sufficient once a pilot memorizes the aircraft's exterior inspection points.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator inside a fuel tester cup reveals water contamination drained from a wing tank sump valve?
What happens to your ground track on a flight simulator course if you fly a magnetic heading without correcting for crosswind drift?
What measurement confirms whether your aircraft is ahead of or behind schedule when crossing a visual checkpoint along your route?
Why is it dangerous to turn a propeller by hand during a preflight inspection without verifying the magnetos are switched off?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Runway numbers represent the runway's magnetic compass heading rounded to the nearest ten degrees with the trailing zero omitted.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Airport runways are numbered sequentially starting from 1 based on the chronological order in which they were paved.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Active runways are selected so aircraft take off and land into a headwind, which increases wing lift at lower ground speeds.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Airplanes take off and land with a strong tailwind so the wind pushes the aircraft down the runway faster.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Runways use white markings and white edge lights, whereas taxiways use yellow paint markings, blue edge lights, and green centerline lights.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Yellow markings and blue edge lights identify active runways, while white markings and green centerline lights mark taxiways.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tower controllers manage airport surface and pattern traffic, while TRACON and ARTCC facilities handle radar approach and en route flights.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An Airport Traffic Control Tower controller tracks and vectors high-altitude airliners across multistate en route airways.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does an airport switch its active runway from Runway 09 to Runway 27 during changing weather?
Which physical marking and lighting color distinguish an airport taxiway centerline from an active runway centerline at night?
What measurement determines why a runway aligned with a 268-degree magnetic compass azimuth is painted with the number 27?
Why is it dangerous to taxi an aircraft across double solid yellow hold-short lines without explicit tower clearance?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Private pilots can only share pro-rata trip expenses with passengers; flying for compensation requires a Commercial Pilot Certificate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Private Pilot Certificate allows a pilot to fly passengers for hire and accept full payment for charter flights.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Part 107 remote pilots must stay at or below 400 feet AGL and obtain prior FAA airspace authorization before flying in controlled airspace.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Holding an FAA Remote Pilot Certificate authorizes a drone operator to fly above 400 feet in controlled airspace without approval.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Student pilots are prohibited from carrying passengers on solo flights and must hold specific instructor endorsements for every solo flight.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Student Pilot Certificate permits a trainee to bring family members along on solo cross-country practice flights.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Any private pilot can add an Instrument Rating to fly safely through clouds and low visibility under Instrument Flight Rules.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An Instrument Rating is only useful for commercial airline captains flying large multi-engine jets at high altitudes.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a VFR-only private pilot's legal options when cloud ceilings drop below basic Visual Flight Rules minimums?
Which legal privilege distinguishes a Commercial Pilot Certificate holder from a Private Pilot Certificate holder under FAA rules?
What measurement of logged flight hours and recent takeoffs and landings must a pilot record to carry passengers legally?
Why is it dangerous to fly into clouds without an instrument rating and current proficiency in instrument flight reference?
